In a paired study of 28 project-specific questions across two Unity games, the authors report 53.4% fewer tokens and 51.6% lower wall time than a general-purpose exploration agent using the same model and harness; one project is internal and each question has one run per arm. The study measures navigation cost, not coding correctness or software quality, and has not been independently reproduced here.
items.title: Unity Insight reports lower agent navigation cost on two Unity projects

items.content_text: The EBRL preprint describes a system built on RLinf that overlaps rollout with model training, pipelines simulation and generation, schedules environment work asynchronously, and reallocates CPU cores and GPU streaming multiprocessors as stage demands change. Across five simulator-policy configurations and several accelerator testbeds, the authors report 1.30×–3.47× end-to-end trajectory throughput over compared embodied-RL systems. Their ablations report that removing resource allocation, group pipelining or asynchronous execution reduces throughput. These are author-reported simulation results; no independent rerun or physical-robot evaluation was performed here.
tags: Institute for AI Industry Research, Tsinghua University
Nanjing University of Posts and Telecommunications
University of Science and Technology of China
items.title: EBRL reports 1.30×–3.47× higher throughput for simulated embodied-RL training

items.content_text: The arXiv preprint introduces RECAP, which gives GRPO training step-level credit using LLM-annotated semantic dependencies plus a gold-answer likelihood signal. On Qwen2.5-Math-7B, the authors report 2.0–3.7 percentage-point pass@1 gains and 8–31% fewer reasoning tokens than GRPO across GSM8K, MATH-500, AIME 2024 and AIME 2025. Results on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B are mixed, so the paper does not establish a uniform cross-model improvement. These are author-reported experiments, not independently reproduced; the tested regime is limited to two 7B math models and four benchmarks.
items.title: RECAP uses dependency-aware step credit to reduce reasoning tokens in math models

items.content_text: A September 2026 preprint introduces SkillGym, a pipeline that turns human-written agent skills into executable tasks with code-based outcome checks and contrastive skill-dependence labels. The authors report 2,756 environments across 12 categories and 8,364 successful trajectories, then fine-tune Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on SkillGym trajectories. They report gains on GDPval-AA v2, Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SkillsBench, including performance that persists without inference-time skills. These remain paper-reported results. The paper’s v2 abstract and v2 HTML disagree on the no-skills SkillsBench gain (12.38 versus 14.68 points), and the reported benchmark comparisons depend on specific harnesses; code, dataset and model artifacts were not audited in this review.
items.title: SkillGym reports agent training gains from executable human-workflow environments

items.content_text: A 13 October preprint introduces Tev-Gym, a 1,170-environment synthetic training corpus with hidden latent-world specifications, strict task verifiers and staged progress scores. The authors use progress-potential reward shaping to train Qwen3.5-9B and Qwen3.8-27B, reporting higher scores than their base checkpoints on Agents’ Last Exam’s computing-and-math subset (ALE-CM). Tev-27B’s reported Pass@5 is 0.28 versus 0.17 for its base and equals the paper’s reported GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5 values under the listed harness. The authors also report transfer to selected Terminal-Bench computing-and-math subsets and a larger GLM-5.3-Flash model. These are author-reported results; this review did not independently reproduce them, and the project page lists code and data as forthcoming.
items.title: Tev reports long-horizon agent training gains from verified environments and dense progress rewards

items.content_text: A European Commission press release dated 9 October 2026 announced a special meeting of the AI Act Scientific Panel on frontier AI safety and security risks. In a Spanish-language follow-up published 12 October, the Commission says the meeting addressed recent loss-of-control incidents, model monitorability and recursive self-improvement; it summarizes four recommendations, including governance of internal-model risks, stronger incident-investigation capacity, international information sharing and scrutiny of training techniques that reduce monitorability. The Commission also says it will send combined questions to developers as it investigates incidents. The sources do not identify the incidents or models, publish the questions, or establish that the recommendations became binding policy. This is a first-party account of advisory work, not independent incident verification.
items.title: EU Commission schedules special scientific-panel meeting on frontier AI risks after reported loss-of-control investigations

items.content_text: GroundedGEO studies whether generative search rankers can elevate relevant-looking product text without evidence support. In a 50-query e-commerce benchmark, the authors report an unsupported-rich ranking gain on frozen Qwen2.5-7B, with the effect marginal on one other ranker and absent on a third. An oracle-label reranker reduced attack-arm top-three rates in the paper's controlled experiment, but every tested automatic judge failed a preregistered reliability gate and the human-gold arm has unresolved interpretation. The authors do not establish a validated automatic defense or a web-wide effect.
items.title: GroundedGEO tests evidence-aware ranking against unsupported but relevant-looking text

items.content_text: The CC-OPD preprint proposes assigning token-level training signals to individual instruction constraints by comparing a frozen teacher's scores with and without each constraint. In experiments reported by the authors, CC-OPD had the highest average among the tested methods across seven benchmarks and two Qwen model pairs; a Qwen2.5-1.5B student exceeded its GRPO-IR-trained 7B teacher on MulDimIF. These are preprint-reported outcomes, not independently reproduced results, and the evidence covers only the tested models and training setup.
items.title: CC-OPD uses counterfactual teacher scores to improve multi-constraint instruction following

items.content_text: Senators Michael Bennet and Peter Welch announced a proposal for a Federal Digital Commission with oversight powers spanning frontier AI and large digital platforms. Their press release describes proposed pre-certification, a possible pause of certain high-risk model releases, incident-reporting and mitigation duties, and civil penalties up to 15% of prior-year global revenue. This is a proposal described by its sponsors, not an introduced or enacted law; the underlying legislative text was not located in this review.
items.title: Bennet and Welch propose a federal agency with pre-release AI review authority

items.content_text: The October 2026 X-AgentRed preprint uses a graph of tool effects and execution preconditions to generate cross-service red-team scenarios, then uses execution feedback to diversify successful paths and repair blocked ones. In one evaluation run per configuration across four target agents in a simulated ecosystem of 30 services and 914 tools, the authors report a 19.2% harmful-path rate, versus 10.5% for STAC and 2.7% for TRACE; average tool coverage is 41.5%, versus 13.9% and 23.7%. These are paper-reported simulator results, not estimates of real-world agent risk.
items.title: Graph-guided red-teaming finds more harmful cross-service paths in a simulated personal-agent ecosystem

items.content_text: A September 2026 preprint defines a positive energy defect for a periodic-cube, unforced Leray–Hopf solution at fixed viscosity and reports a Lean 4 formal reduction: the defect is equivalent to a uniform positive lower bound on time-averaged energy flux through all sufficiently fine dyadic Fourier shells. The paper gives necessary admissibility conditions and argues that finite Galerkin computation cannot witness the required uniform ceiling; its 12 pseudo-spectral runs at 128³ and 256³ meet a temporal flux condition but fail to sustain the floor toward the Kolmogorov scale. This is a bounded mathematical search specification, not an unforced singularity result. The authors state that their Lean library contains no Navier–Stokes object and does not connect the reduction to a separately formalized Leray–Hopf theory; the target remains open.
items.title: A Lean-formalized search target for the open unforced Navier–Stokes problem
